function: Joint transmit beamforming and STAR-RIS transmission/reflection phase-shift design maximizing normalized communication rate plus target illumination (sensing) power in an ISAC system (p. 3).
system: STAR-RIS-assisted ISAC: BS ULA with N=4 antennas, STAR-RIS UPA with 3x3 elements (size swept in Figs. 3-4), M=4 users, K=3 targets; frequency band not stated (pp. 2-5).
method: Meta-SAC: soft actor-critic reinforcement learning with MAML meta-learning; meta-training over tasks of random user and target locations, then meta-adaptation to a new environment (p. 4).
data_channel: Self-defined simulation: array-response channels with path loss, STAR-RIS-to-user LoS, Rician BS-to-STAR-RIS link (kappa=10); users and targets random within 2 m circles; CSI known at BS (pp. 2-4).
test_conditions: Meta-training on tasks with random user and target positions; test in a different environment after meta-adaptation, or the same one (no-mismatch); RIS size swept (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned only: DDPG and PPO [8]; meta-SAC variants with and without mismatch. No non-learned baseline such as random or fixed RIS, or optimization (p. 4, Figs. 1-4).
metrics: Mean reward (normalized rate plus sensing power), effective sensing power, total minimum achievable rate, versus episodes, RIS elements, and total minimum rate (Figs. 1-4, pp. 4-5).
complexity: Orders of complexity for training and running modes: sum over layers of h_l h_(l+1) times data, steps, tasks, episodes, Eqs. (21)-(22); no runtime reported (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "the channel matrix between the STAR-RIS and BS is assumed as Rician fading". Missing: no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel; the links are self-defined with path loss and steering vectors (pp. 2-4).
q2_support: p. 4: "meta-SAC with different training and testing environments". This mismatch case uses the meta-adaptation phase started from the meta-trained parameters; tasks differ by random user and target locations (p. 4).
q3_support: p. 4: "we compare it with the traditional DDPG and proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithms". Missing: no non-learned baseline in the text or in Figs. 1-4; the meta-SAC variants do not count as baselines.
q4_support: p. 4: "the complexity in the running mode is computed as follows". Eqs. (21)-(22) give the O() order for the training and running modes.
q5_support: p. 4: "We consider a BS equipped with N = 4 antennas positioned at the origin (0, 0, 0)". Self-defined simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included, area 5: the learned meta-SAC agent outputs the BS beamformers and the STAR-RIS phase shifts for an objective that adds communication rate and target illumination power (p. 3), so ISAC wins over area 3 by the tie-break order. q2 is 1 because the paper tests meta-SAC in an environment different from training after meta-adaptation (p. 4), but it only describes the environments as distinct random locations of users and targets, so the reviewer may want to confirm that this is a new condition. q3 is 0: DDPG and PPO are learned baselines, but no non-learned method is compared. The frequency band is not stated; perfect CSI at the BS is assumed (p. 3).
